And we had touched on some of the history that had occurred during the time of Muawiyah and most notably some of the disagreements which occurred between Muawiyah and Ali ibn Abi Talib radi allahu anhu. But Muawiyah was not alone in this amongst the companions of the prophet sallallahu alaihi wasallam. He spearheaded the effort in order to fulfill the aspect of the truth that he felt was most correct and Muawiyah radi Allahu anhu is not you know, some small potatoes. Muawiyah radi Allahu anhu is a major scholar from amongst the companions radi Allahu anhu. And I only mention this because many of us have heard parts of this story, but most of us have misunderstood most of the parts that we've heard. And I say this from experience. if I were to just take a tally on me growing up and what I've heard from people around me and the elders in my family and in my community growing up, we were taught a very askewed view on the way that the Muslimin are to view and to hold the difference of opinion which resulted in infighting and bloodshed amongst the companions radi Allahu anhu. The position of Ahlus Sunnah, the position of Ahlus Sunnah is as summarized by by Al-Qahtani rahimahullah in his Nuniyah, yaqulu da'ma jara bayna al-sahabati fil waga bisuyufihim yawm al taqal jama'ani faqatiluhum minhum wa qatiluhum lahum wakilahuma fil hashri marhumani. He says, "Do not discuss and debate the sides of the issue which occurred between the companions radi Allahu anhu when it culminated in actual physical battle." And he says, rahimahullah, "That the one amongst the companions, any of the companions that was killed during that disagreement, he is a companion. And anyone who killed during that disagreement is also a companion. That is their close circle. We're not part of that. We don't get to judge them. We're not companions of the prophet Sallallahu alaihi wasallam. And both of them, both sides entirely, every companion that had anything to do with the disagreement or those who refrained from become involving themselves in the disagreements, all of the companions will be forgiven on the day of judgement because they are between two rewards and one reward. As the prophet Sallallahu alaihi wasallam says in that Hakim, either just had a fact for a Sabah for a who a jar what either a star for a who a jar and one word. He says that if a judge tries his best to to judge with the truth and what is correct and he makes a judgement and he is correct in said judgement, he will be rewarded twofold. And if he is wrong, he will be rewarded at least one. And so the companions of Allah and them, they had this disagreement and it as we mentioned yesterday, very simply, if we were to put it very simply, what happened? Uthman and them was attacked by a group of young impressionable men that came from both Iraq and from Egypt. And they had very unsavory origins. And they had been inoculated with a kind of arrogance and anger and hatred towards Uthman ibn Affan, radiya Allahu anhu. They accused him of being unjust. They accused him of taking the Khilafah and making it his own. They accused him of giving positions of power to his family members, right? Nepotism and cronyism. The question here is is it wrong? Let's say I was a a person of authority, a a person in a position of power, right? Is it inherently wrong for me to make my brother in a position of power with me? Is that wrong? No. When is it wrong? When that's what put him in that position. Meaning, he's not qualified for that position, but I put him in that position anyways. That is nepotism. That is what is haram. But if my family member happens to be happens to be qualified, that actually might be better for me to put him in that position because it is closer to keeping a harmonious level-headedness to the government. So, there's an issue of ijtihad. But they came and they resorted Uthman to his house. They prohibited him from coming out of his house. They attacked him and those around him of the companions. they were armed. And they kept him in his house for a number of days, and they finally murdered him. It it culminated in his murder. And it's said that he was murdered just before the Adhan of Maghrib while he was reading the Quran. At the edges of the Muslim empire. Remember we said they came from Egypt and they came from Iraq, right? Right at the edges of those two major empires that were just defeated by Umar radiyallahu anhu the Romans and the Persians. summary: This lecture discusses the historical disputes between the companions of the Prophet Muhammad, particularly focusing on Muawiyah ibn Abi Sufyan and his disagreements with Ali ibn Abi Talib following the murder of Caliph Uthman ibn Affan. The speaker explains that these companions had different approaches to addressing Uthman's assassination—Muawiyah wanted immediate execution of the perpetrators while Ali believed this would destabilize the newly-formed caliphate. The lecturer emphasizes the Islamic scholarly position (Ahlus Sunnah) that Muslims should not judge or debate these internal disputes among the companions, as they are all considered righteous and will be forgiven. The speaker also discusses Abdullah ibn Saba, a Jewish infiltrator who radicalized young Muslims and is credited as the spiritual grandfather of both the Khawarij and Rafidah (Shia) movements.
